goal: Move the Spec-binding precondition from freeze time to enrollment time: extract boundSpecPath and readBoundActiveSpec into runtime/kernel/spec_binding.ts and have runtime/kernel/enrollment.ts reject a scope_hint that lacks the bound active and archive Spec paths, naming each missing path, while retaining freeze-time enforcement unchanged.

acceptance.assertion: A new module runtime/kernel/spec_binding.ts owns boundSpecPath and readBoundActiveSpec. Given a repository root and a scope_hint it returns the resolved bound active Spec path or a structured rejection naming each missing required path. It fails closed on zero bound Specs and on more than one, and the existing freeze-time message `artifact freeze requires one scope-bound active Spec` is preserved for the freeze caller.

runtime/kernel/enrollment.ts calls the shared function inside the existing enrollment transaction and refuses an enrollment whose scope_hint omits the bound active Spec path or its archive path, reporting each missing path by name. The check is a pure read that writes nothing, adds no second human gate, and is idempotent: re-running it on unchanged inputs returns the same projection.

Freeze-time enforcement is retained rather than replaced, because enrollment cannot observe post-implementation scope drift: runtime/kernel/canary_application.ts still validates the binding at freeze with unchanged behavior, and a task whose scope drifts after enrollment is still refused at freeze.

The restriction is deliberate and observable: an existing candidate TaskIntent whose scope_hint omits the Spec paths stops enrolling and must be revised, and the refusal names the exact paths to add rather than reporting a generic validation failure.
